$comment: Every number GoVIRAL's signal score depends on lives here and nowhere else. The three components are deliberately incomparable readings kept apart until the last step: relative growth is a ratio, absolute volume is normalized inside its own source kind, and breadth counts operators rather than adding their units together.
$statusComment: explodingScore is reached on the renormalized 0-100 score; peakedGrowth is the decline at which a signal is called peaked whatever its score; breakoutPercent is Google Trends' own Breakout marker, above which relative growth is pinned to its ceiling.
$providerComment: sourceKinds picks the half-life band; independenceGroups is what makes breadth mean independent sources. Two Google surfaces are one operator, and Instagram and Threads are one operator, so neither pair can manufacture breadth on its own.
$windowComment: halfLifeHours is the window a reading is good for; maximumHours is how long storm re-triggers may keep one alive since it was first flagged. format-shift is configured for the 30-90 day band the brief names; nothing in this repository feeds it beyond the scout's own format counts.
$volumeComment: One ceiling per source kind, because a search-traffic estimate, an article count and a hashtag's post count are different units. A single shared ceiling would be the merged number the founding decision refuses.
